title: Callable Discriminator must resolve definition-refs on both paths (handler vs definitions dict)
answers: callable discriminator fails with PEP 695 type alias in Field(discriminator=...)
TypeAliasType union with Tag not recognized when discriminator is a function
MissingDefinitionForUnionRef with Discriminator(lambda ...) on a type alias field
body:
Symptom: a field typed as a PEP 695 / TypeAliasType union of `Annotated[Model, Tag(...)]` choices, with `Field(discriminator=Discriminator(callable))`, failed to validate because the tags were not found or the ref was not resolved. `Annotated[..., Discriminator(...)]` worked.
Root cause: `pydantic/types.py:Discriminator._convert_schema` only resolved `definition-ref` schemas (the root and each choice) through `handler.resolve_ref_schema`. When it is called later from `pydantic/_internal/_discriminated_union.py:apply_discriminator` (deferred/callable discriminators), `handler` is None, so refs were never resolved.
Fix pattern: `apply_discriminator` now passes `definitions=definitions`. `_convert_schema` uses a local `_resolve_ref` helper that tries `handler` first and falls back to `definitions.get(schema['schema_ref'])`. A root ref that can't be resolved raises `MissingDefinitionForUnionRef`. A choice ref that can't be resolved is left as it is.
Constraints: any new ref-dependent logic in `_convert_schema` has to go through `_resolve_ref`, never `handler` directly, because both entry points exist (during field schema generation and deferred via `apply_discriminator`). This mirrors `_ApplyInferredDiscriminator._apply_to_root()` for string discriminators. Nested refs are still not flattened (there is an xfail test).
applies: Discriminated unions with callable Discriminator in pydantic/types.py and pydantic/_internal/_discriminated_union.py
